hook.text: 99% of vanilla flavor used worldwide is synthetic vanillin. Real vanilla beans supply barely 1% of demand.

buildup.text: Vanilla orchids require hand-pollination and months of curing. Real vanilla costs $250–600 per kilogram.

discovery.text: Vanillin was first synthesized from pine tree sap in 1874. Today most comes from guaiacol, a petrochemical.

twist.text: Biotech companies now ferment vanillin from sugar using yeast. It's labeled 'natural flavor' despite being lab-made.

climax.text: Madagascar produces 80% of real vanilla. Price swings devastate farmers who can't compete with synthetics.

punchline.text: Your vanilla ice cream likely never met a vanilla bean.

quiz.question: What percentage of the world's vanilla flavor is synthetic?
